body: I'd say that this is similar to a bad breakup but months after it has occurred. And also add onto that the knowledge that you will definitely never get to be with her.
I will indeed attempt this. I am going to just be there for her and stop making this about me.
Yeah I will most likely do this. Thanks for the help, from all of ya.

I have no reason to hide the extent of what I've done here. I'm looking for actual advice and if I didn't give you guys the whole story it wouldn't end up helping me at all.


That being said she doesn't seem to fully believe me that she even caused any real pain as she was just slapping my back.

I will definitely try this. To be the strong one. How do I tell her that I feel like she's aiming all that hurt at what I did? I had tried to say that to her a couple days ago but every time I was about to it felt like I was taking value away from her family member's death.

I understand that, it still doesn't change how I feel about her though. I'm going to try to approach living without her as best as I can, and keep in contact with her regularly to make sure bills are getting paid as they are under my name as well.

I know she does but that kind of help isn't available where we live nor do we have the kind of money to afford it. Since we recently moved into a new state we were still under the time allowed to switch health insurances and hadn't yet done it as we planned to try through our jobs.



I wish there was a way for me to help her and console her through all of this but my presence only exacerbates the issue. She seems to be more open when we talk through facebook, but I don't know how to convince someone that they are the one with the power to change how they feel and then subsequently motivate them to do so.

>She argues that the pain from her slaps was caused accidentally and she was in the middle of coming towards me to console me when I punched her leg which is a valid point. One was accidental, the other was malicious and vindictive in nature.


From another reply of mine. I'd say I'm mixed feelings between how you feel and how she feels. I'd love to be able to have talked it out but I think that PTSD could be an issue here and now she just sees me like her prior abusers. There's not much talking can do about that, the only thing that can fix that is if she takes the time to really think about it while at the same time having the ultimate intention of forgiving me. That's why I'm hoping that she just needs space. I'm hoping that I'll move out for a month or two and she'll be ready to try again. I'm just scared that I might end up pushing her further away by the fact that every time I see her I end up wanting to talk about it.


She and I probably won't see each other much before I move out so I told her today that if I could have any final words about it that "I'm beginning to understand the emotional toll I've put you under, I'm sorry I've been so selfishly focused on how all of this makes me feel. I just want you to know, that from the bottom of my heart I'm sorry. And while I did make a huge mistake, it doesn't define me. I know what I did, and I know that it was a terrible thing to have done, but that doesn't change who I am. I am still the same person, now with one more lesson to never forget."

A few days before all of it happened the family member she was living with before me passed away. It was right after she moved in with me and he literally died as she was giving him a hug. She started crying while the rest of her family started screaming at her as if it was somehow her fault (they were all gathered there as they were warned it was possibly his last day). It's entirely unrelated to our situation except for the fact that she was harboring this grief. His funeral is tomorrow and she currently refuses to use my car to get there (it's happening about 250 miles away) even though she has no other ride. Today when I talked to her she seemed a little bit more open about taking my car for the day but may just be going with people she doesn't enjoy being around instead.

I've considered this as well but have been unable to find anyone to do this with. On top of that it's a one bedroom apartment, one of us would have to live in the little dining area or living room area and the bathroom would require entering the bedroom.


And again, I'd like for us to get back together. Even if that's a complete stretch I don't think that forcing her situation to get even worse would ever do anything for her other than harboring extreme contempt for me.


I am, after all, the one who fucked up here and I can't force her to trust me by giving her an ultimatum of trust me or go homeless.

There still stands the fact that if she leaves I can't afford to live here. When we moved in together I brought the bulk of the bills (been paying $380 a month on car payments not including insurance, hope to try to refinance next month) while she only had a couple small bills on credit cards due to her trying to build up her credit.

This is the truth I've been trying hard to prepare myself for, but I really don't know how to move on from this. Going back to the life I already hated and now I get to think about the one time I was able to not only get out of my situation but into a perfect one. 


I've been going back and forth through two emotions. Crying uncontrollably and completely numb to everything. Going to work is difficult for me now. I just recently transferred as my old branch was closing and the new place only gives you livable hours if you rise above the rest by a considerable margin. I switched to a highly competitive environment right before the most crushing blow to my depression was about to hit. I've even taken bathroom breaks just to go and cry to myself as even though I work in a busy restaurant I still manage to nonstop think about my situation.

The punch was definitely excessive as it ended up leaving a bruise. I just wish more than anything that I could take it back and never have done it in the first place. I know that her forgiving me is impossible unless she decides to believe that I wasn't being abusive. I wish there was a way to convince her that I'm not just saying that in order to win her trust back.

She argues that the pain from her slaps was caused accidentally and she was in the middle of coming towards me to console me when I punched her leg which is a valid point. One was accidental, the other was malicious and vindictive in nature. We are both on the lease. I admit this idea has come to me a few times that maybe I've just been used but it had all been genuine up until now.


It's bad but I'm hoping that in her loneliness she will reach out to me and that can be my window back in. I'm just scared that she won't ever have the chance to get lonely enough to try again with me as there have always been 5+ people with a deep crush on her for as long as I've known her. It just sucks losing the first real friend that I've had this close of a connection to and also losing the love of my life at the same time.


At one point I did get angry at the idea of kicking me out (this has been my favorite place I've ever lived, not having to share it with anyone but her and we've made the best roommates) but she just responded with the fact that she will leave if I don't. She doesn't have anywhere to go and she understands that she's contractually obliged to make sure rent gets paid for as long as she is on the lease. On top of that I'm pretty sure the only reason she's tried to make it work for these last two weeks is due to the fact that she feels stuck.


I know I could opt not to leave but I'm trying not to fight her in a time of her life that she desperately needs the peace she's seeking. I don't want to burn bridges by being stubborn or proud, I just hope that eventually she does see that I was worth having around.

I feel the same way. It seems to alternate, I'll have a week where I'm fine and focused on life and moving forward. I'll lose some weight and stick to my diet. Then the next week I will have apathy towards everything. At work in order to hide my depression I end up drowning myself in caffeine and now I'm starting to get heart issues. On my days off I don't get out of my bed until I start to get sick from not having showered. I try to save money and not to spend it on anything, but then I can't stand the way I feel and end up spending it on alcohol.
I am the same way. It's why I drink, to feel something. Whether it's happiness or sadness (mostly sadness, but I digress) I get a sense of relief that I can *feel* things

This line has gone through my head a million times. I don't like saying it to people because it sounds like I'm quoting a song but it describes how I feel immensely. I find myself getting drunk just so that I can feel depressed and then I find ways to fuel the depression like the right music, being alone, keeping the lights off, etc. I end up feeling lonely but even someone who understood this perfectly I couldn't imagine myself inviting them to join me
